prerequisites.title: Xero developer account and app
prerequisites.detail: Register an app to get a client ID and secret; OAuth 2.0 is required for new integrations.

prerequisites.title: Demo company or Xero subscription
prerequisites.detail: Xero says you can develop at no cost on its demo company or a trial or paid organisation.

prerequisites.title: 10 beta customers
prerequisites.detail: Xero's blog says a new app must onboard 10 beta customers before the certification form unlocks. Each must be a real organisation, not a demo company, with API calls in the last 30 days.

steps.title: Register your Xero app
steps.detail: Log in to the Xero developer portal, create the app and note the client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: You hold a client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Check and register the redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard; it must be absolute with no wildcards. Up to 50 are allowed.
steps.done_when: The URI is saved in the Xero app.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config for the xero toolkit via Composio's API with your own client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection works.

steps.title: Test on the demo company
steps.detail: Connect the demo company and run your agent's main calls.
steps.done_when: The core flows work end to end.

steps.title: Draft security assessment answers
steps.detail: Prepare answers on authentication, encryption, personnel security and audit logging for you to check.
steps.done_when: A draft covers each requirement area.

steps.title: Submit the security assessment
steps.detail: Confirm the answers are true and submit them to Xero.

steps.title: Xero reviews the assessment
steps.detail: Review takes 5-10 working days; Xero emails the result. If you fail, you get a remediation report with 30 days for a plan and 60 to implement.

steps.title: Apply to the App Partner Program
steps.detail: Apply, onboard 10 beta customers and complete certification.

steps.title: Prepare listing and Sign Up with Xero
steps.detail: Write clear listing content and implement Sign Up with Xero before submitting.
steps.done_when: Listing draft is ready and sign-up works.

steps.title: Xero reviews your listing
steps.detail: Xero reviews the submitted listing; duration is not documented.

traps.title: Unapproved app capped at 25 clients
traps.detail: A developer reported a 25-client cap before app partner approval, which blocks rollout. Start the approval process before launch.

traps.title: Wrong Sign Up/Sign In labels delay certification
traps.detail: One developer report names wrong button labelling as a common cause of delay; it also says certification needs nine checkpoints plus ten customers.

traps.title: Remediation can add up to 90 days
traps.detail: If you fail, you get 30 days to plan and 60 days to implement, then Xero re-reviews.

traps.title: 1,000 connections triggers a harder review
traps.detail: At 1,000 or more connections you must pass an advanced assessment.

traps.title: The assessment repeats every year
traps.detail: Plan the assessment as a yearly task.

traps.title: Managed app is not available
traps.detail: Composio has no managed Xero app, so you cannot prototype without your own credentials.

blockers.symptom: Cannot connect more than about 25 customers
blockers.what_it_means: Developers report an unapproved app is capped until Xero approves it as an app partner.
blockers.what_to_do: Start the security assessment and partner approval process with Xero.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft assessment answers and track the checklist.

blockers.what_it_means: The assessment did not pass; you have 30 days for a plan and 60 days to fix.
blockers.what_to_do: Write the remediation plan, implement the fixes and request re-review.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the remediation plan from the report.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: A custom auth config lets the developer supply their own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default whenever they are available for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With a managed app, users see the Composio name on the OAuth consent screen, not the developer's app name.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Managed apps request Composio's default scopes, which may not cover everything a developer needs, so custom scopes require the developer's own app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share their rate-limit quota across all Composio users, while a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; a developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still [white-label the Connect Link page](/docs/authentication/white-labeling-authentication#customizing-the-connect-link) with your logo and app title without needing your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: The page says managed apps are fine for prototypes and internal tools, and that a developer can white-label the Connect Link page with their logo and app title without their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Enterprise customers require your branding end-to-end.
evidence.answer: Enterprise customers who require the developer's branding end-to-end are a case where the developer should use their own app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants of an app, such as a private Salesforce subdomain, need their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: You will now be required to onboard 10 beta customers prior to submitting your application via your app in the developer centre.
evidence.answer: Xero's official blog (May 2025) says a new app must onboard 10 beta customers before the certification application form is unlocked; a beta customer must not be a demo company and must have made API calls to its tenant in the last 30 days.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: The issue is Xero has a limit of 25 clients connected to our app until we become an
evidence.answer: Developer report (Retool forum, June 2025): before app partner approval, an unapproved Xero app is capped at 25 connected clients, which blocks customer rollout.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: They’ll up the cap to 100 users, then above a 100 is more thorough in their questioning and review, beyond 1000 is a much more thorough process.
evidence.answer: Developer report (DannyF, Retool forum, June 2025): Xero's approval includes a visual walkthrough/app interview, lifts the cap to 100 users, applies deeper review of API call history above 100, and a much more thorough process beyond 1,000.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: You'll need to pass all nine — plus have ten customers using your app — before Xero will certify it.
evidence.answer: Developer report (Remittance Go, 2026): certification requires passing nine required checkpoints plus having ten customers using the app; the author names wrong Sign Up/Sign In button labelling as a common cause of certification delays.
